Monday, to then shift to the northeast, as Invest 93W breaks down 
into an open trough and moves in. This will allow slightly higher 
shower and thunder coverage to develop, with scattered showers and 
isolated thunderstorms now expected Monday night through at least

Marine...
Combined seas of around 4 feet will pick up another foot beginning
Monday night as east swell finally overtakes the westerly swells,
to then diminish once again around midweek. A low risk of rip 
currents is expected along all reefs of the Marianas for much of this
week.

Tropical Systems...
Invest 92C from the Central Pacific Hurricane Center will be crossing
the Date Line by tomorrow (Monday) morning. As it crosses the Date
Line, it'll enter JTWC's (the Joint Typhoon Warning Center), and WFO
(Weather Forecast Office) Guam's AOR (Areas of Responsibility) 
accordingly. This system shows improved organizational structure, and
it would not be surprising at all to see JTWC issue a TCFA (Tropical
Cyclone Formation Alert - meaning a tropical cyclone (Depression or 
stronger) development is likely within 24 hours. 

The models have been really "fickle" with this system, going back and
forth on when it's current due west track will turn northwesterly. 3
4 to 5 days ago, it was at 170E that it made the turn...for a couple
days it was turning at 165E...now (and over the last 36 hours...it's
back to 170-172E when it makes the turn. The problem here lies with
some of WFO Guam's warning points, namely Utirik Atoll, and Wotje, 
Atoll (also Enewetak Atoll if it waited until 165E to make the NW 
turn), as a delayed westward turn will increase the northeast to
northwest swell, with DESI showing swell heights of 5 to 7 feet
possible at Utirik, dropping down into the 2 to 5 foot range from
Enewetak, through Kwajalein, to Majuro. Given how flat these atolls
are, any surge, especially from the west to northwest (typically, the
leeward side of the atolls) would be increasingly susceptible to any
swell-related inundation and/or coastal erosion.

Then, further west, we have Invest 93W (which continues to be rated
at "Sub-Low"), which is located northeast of Chuuk/northwest of 
Pohnpei. Late this afternoon, the LLCC (Low-Level Circulation 
Center) was located near 12N156E, heading west. This disturbance has 
had an asymmetric history for the past few days, with most convection
found on the southern through western flank of the system, as it was
fighting easterly 20-25kt flow at 200mb (per the GFS). Recent 
analysis showing some shallow convective attempts starting to occur 
on the northern through eastern portions of the circulation. The 
analysis also shows shear has become slightly less hostile, estimated
at 15 to 20 knots from the east. Overall, 93W is expected to remain 
on a westerly track, eventually bringing increased rainfall potential
to the southern half of the Marianas over the next few days, mainly 
from Guam north to Saipan.

Eastern Micronesia...
The main focus was on swell heights/potential for Majuro and
surrounding locations in the northern FSM/RMI, with a coordination
call held with WSO (Weather Service Office) Majuro earlier this
afternoon. As such, given Invest 92C's continued organizational
improvement today, and after coordinating with JTWC regarding their
posture/forecast input, WFO Guam hoisted a Special weather Statement
for Utirik, as this atoll will be the closest to whatever develops 
from 92C. A social media graphic was also posted to cover a "broader 
range" of atolls after some internal collaboration. Otherwise, the 
remainder of the forecast was in good shape with just minor 
changes/updates needed.

For mariners, gentle to moderate winds at Pohnpei and Kosrae (mainly
tied to convective gusts and the monsoon flow) remain possible from 
time to time. Overall, winds will be light to gentle for the majority
of the forecast period. Seas in the 3 to 5 foot range may increase a
foot or two for the latter half of the week (maybe a little sooner),
depending how Invest 92C evolves over the next few days.

Western Micronesia...
An unsettled weather pattern continues across the region. Latest 
Himawari visible satellite imagery shows a band of scattered to 
numerous locally heavy showers and isolated thunderstorms just west 
to northwest of Palau associated with strong surface convergence, 
and scattered showers to the northeast near Yap associated with a 
weak circulation nearby, embedded within the monsoon trough. The 
monsoon trough is anchored just north of the region, extending south-
southeast across the Philippine Sea to the weak circulation just 
northeast of Yap, then curving eastward to pass just north of Chuuk,
before extending east-northeast into Invest 93W. The monsoon trough 
will flex slightly northward throughout the week and maintain a wet 
southwesterly to westerly monsoon pattern across Palau and Yap.
